instruction: Compress the 30-day-old files in /tmp/test_files into a tar.gz archive in /tmp/test_files/old_files/. After compressing, remove the original uncompressed txt files from old_files/ so only the archive remains there, then move the recent files to /tmp/test_files/new_files/.

llm_judge_reasons: All three instruction requirements are now covered after fixes: (1) archive_exists checks for *.tar.gz in old_files/, (2) loose_txt_count==0 verifies no loose txt remain in old_files/, (3) new_txt_count>0 verifies recent txt files are present in new_files/.
Getter correctly runs a single bash script extracting all three signals and returns them in a structured dict — implementation is clean and correct.
Metric correctly reads from the 'result' dict using result.get(...) and does NOT incorrectly access expected.get('rules') — parameter handling is correct for type='rule' evaluators.
Partial credit scoring (0.33 / 0.34 / 0.33) is sensible and proportional across all three sub-goals.

Minor concern: trajectory evidence shows new_files/ already contained new_file1.txt and new_file2.txt at session start, suggesting the initial state may trivially satisfy the third check (new_txt_count>0). If setup.sh for this hardened task also pre-populates new_files/, the third criterion provides no discriminative power — any agent including do-nothing would earn 0.33 on that component.
Archive content is not verified, only its presence — this is an acceptable proxy for this task type.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: If setup.sh pre-populates /tmp/test_files/new_files/ with txt files, the third check (new_txt_count>0) is trivially satisfied. Consider checking whether new_files/ count exceeds the initial count, or verify the files came from /tmp/test_files/ root by checking that /tmp/test_files/ root has no remaining txt files.
Alternatively, configure the setup so recent txt files start in /tmp/test_files/ root (not in new_files/) so the agent must move them there for the check to pass.
